operations.comment: ; Fixed CNROM PRG execution view: physical 8 KiB banks [0,1,2,3].
; Execution equates name CPU addresses; *_Storage labels identify emitted physical bytes.
; Forced z:/a: widths and all original .org/.reloc fragments are retained for fidelity.
; WorkPointer0/1/2 and ScratchByte0..F ($B0..$BF) are reused; functional entry comments define
; their local contracts. PrimaryWork/SecondaryWork aliases share storage but have
; separate layouts; names follow each consumer and do not imply original source names. $40..$5F is a shared entity record, not one global layout:
; primary records are 32 bytes, secondary records are 24. Projectile scratch $10..$13
; is status/type/direction-speed/lifetime. Numeric bytes with unresolved roles retain
; their addresses rather than acquire speculative game meanings. Branch-only symbols
; combine their enclosing function and the local mechanical operation; address suffixes
; distinguish shared control-flow joins. Instruction-sized emission regions are not
; original routine boundaries or proof that every static path is naturally reached.
; Shared storage aliases; entry comments specify their local work-record/PPU contracts.
; Round002 consumer-established data identities.
; Round002 mechanically established entries and branch joins.
; Consumer-established table/register identities; no extra table extent is implied.
; Shared scratch, work-record and APU mirror identities.
; Shared interior entries used by classified callers.
; Score, synchronization, CNROM and audio execution addresses.
; Secondary motion, stage transitions, trigger streams and display execution addresses.
; Shared entity animation and secondary entity execution addresses.
; Inventory and entity lifecycle execution addresses.
; Gameplay, movement and projectile execution addresses.
; Stage map and buffer helper execution addresses.
; Reviewed continuation: absolute execution symbols, storage labels remain physical.
; Hardware and evidence-backed RAM identities. Unnamed work bytes retain numeric operands.
; iNES metadata, 16 bytes: magic, 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, CNROM mapper and horizontal mirroring. This is file metadata, outside CPU/PPU storage.
; Four CNROM bank values $00,$01,$02,$03 at CPU $8000. SelectCnromChrBank writes through the corresponding table byte to avoid bus-conflict ambiguity.
; Reset contract: mask IRQs, select binary arithmetic and reset the stack. Disable NMI work while PPU startup settles; clear the small startup work areas before audio/display initialization.
; Initialize the display subsystem, then allow NMI work. PPU control is mirrored in RAM so later uploads restore the same mode.
; NMI preserves A unconditionally. During reset the inhibit byte bypasses all other work; otherwise preserve X/Y and perform one bounded frame service. PRG is fixed CNROM [0,1,2,3].
; The first frame phase copies RAM page $02 to OAM, disables rendering for queued PPU updates, then services attribute and numeric requests. The alternate phase advances audio instead.
; A negative request byte queues six status tiles from $03ED to nametable address $2B36, followed by two zero tiles. Clear the request before uploading.

; Service frame timing, latch controller 1 and shift eight serial button bits into the packed input byte. The OR/rotate sequence accepts either controller data bit wiring; the game button layout is consumed by menu/game handlers.
; Request bits 0/1 select complete 64-byte attribute pages at $23C0/$2BC0. A negative request instead selects a bounded slice using index $68 and length $69. Clear the request after full-page writes.
; Bit $40 of the slice index selects the second nametable. Low six bits select its attribute offset; X retains the buffer index. Caller must supply a nonzero slice length.
; Y supplies the nametable high byte. Reset the PPU address latch and select offset $C0; return X=0 and Y=64 for the upload loop.
; Upload all 32 buffered palette entries to $3F00. The trailing address writes leave the PPU address outside palette access, using the common palette-write cleanup sequence.
; Request bits select up to three two-byte numeric displays. Each passes its digit pair and nametable selector to the shared renderer; the exact on-screen quantities remain unresolved here.
; Enable NMI in the mirrored PPU control and poll PPUSTATUS until vblank. Reset deliberately invokes this several times before ordinary frame synchronization.
; Construct the title/menu display from fixed descriptors, decimal counter digits, column runs and sprite rows. Render with display disabled; frame waits separate later visible menu updates.

; Title column descriptor supplies a solid-run count and, unless that count is 30, an interior span length. Alternating tile values select adjacent columns; each column is padded to 30 writes. Exact artwork meaning remains unresolved.
; For a nonempty interior span, advance the tile by two, read the vertical PPU span and write the saved tile at its far boundary. PPU address increment is selected by the surrounding control setup.
; A second descriptor stream supplies count/high-address/low-address records; zero count terminates. Emit incrementing tile IDs beginning at $70 for each record.
; Enable rendering and build the menu cursor. A stored selection bit adjusts the cursor X field; then poll the menu handler until carry reports acceptance.
; Common display-mode helpers keep RAM mirrors and PPU registers consistent. Entry $8358 accepts control in A and mask in X; entry $835D changes only the mask.
; Mask the packed controller to menu-relevant buttons. Carry reports acceptance; direction changes return carry clear. The previous-button latch prevents repeating a held direction.
; Advance the two-choice selection and move the cursor by 16 pixels, wrapping its Y row. The opposite direction performs the inverse change.
; Latch the direction and play menu sound $2B. Wrap the signed selection into the two-entry domain 0..1.
; Copy the fixed eight-byte sprite seed, then build paired rows of four sprites. Sprite fields use OAM order Y/tile/attributes/X; X advances in four-byte records and columns are eight pixels apart.

; Title display descriptors and encoded tile/attribute runs. BuildTitleAndMenu supplies pointers into this interval. The source stream formats are explained at their consumers; internal artwork boundaries beyond those pointers remain unresolved.
; Selection zero starts a fresh session. The alternate selection retains session counters only when the stored continuation flag permits it; lives reset to three in either case.

; Supported stage initialization entry used by local artificial progression tests. Clear frame/transition state, prepare shared buffers and show a stage banner before loading the world. Runtime evidence requires sprite-zero mode $19=0 at this entry.
; Stages below $1F show a timed banner. Wait for release before accepting skip input; another button opens the status path and re-enters stage initialization. Stages at/above $1F bypass this banner.

; Initialize world, sprite and gameplay buffers through shared loaders. A stage-indexed bitmap enables a random feature variant; preserve zero when the bit is clear. Consumer meaning of the variant at $0724 remains unresolved.
; Reset transient flags before enabling the stage display. Persistent stage/session fields are retained.
; A packed nibble indexed by stage selects an eight-byte background palette in the $DD00 table. Copy it to the palette buffer, then append the shared eight-byte group.
; A second packed stage nibble selects an eight-byte palette at $DC80. Copy it to sprite palette slots $18..$1F and load the shared group at slots $10..$17.

; Decode the stage descriptor at $E3AB into coarse horizontal/vertical starting coordinates and scroll state. The three descriptor ranges choose different scroll origins; then derive collision/attribute coordinates and initialize player fields.

; Select one of sixteen pointer pairs using a packed stage nibble. Store it at $6C/$6D, enable sprite-zero synchronization, start the stage audio request and enter the gameplay loop. Pointer consumer meaning remains unresolved.
; Copy 20 interface palette bytes, set every universal background slot to $0F, and synchronize the palette transition.

; Build the status display using persistent inventory fields $03D3..$03DC. Text tokens index grouped strings; bit-packed item ownership and health information determine which labels and icons appear. Exact item names remain unresolved.
; Low three bits of the upgrade field determine the bounded number of displayed entries. Clamp the special sixth entry and draw successive labels one row apart.
; Two low bits select an inventory group and its row count. Three packed ownership bytes supply a three-bit value per row; show the corresponding two-token item name when nonzero.

; Each of three persistent flag bits selects a special two-token status label. An upgrade threshold adds another label. Ordinary status screens wait for button release and a new face/start input; the fourth-loop display returns immediately.
; Zero flag returns. Otherwise find the set bit, convert it to a two-token table offset and append the label at the next status row.
; Copy the saved row cursor to the text cursor and advance the saved cursor by one 32-tile nametable row.
; Save the current text cursor as the row origin for subsequent inventory lines.
; Advance both the saved origin and the active text cursor by 32 tiles, carrying into the nametable high byte.
; Four OAM descriptors in Y/tile/attribute/X order, copied by the status-screen setup. These bytes describe sprite arrangement, not executable instructions.
; Collect one indexed bit from each of three persistent bytes into the low three bits of $BC. $BA is the inventory column index.
; Shift the selected inventory bit into the result accumulator; callers supply the field byte in A and bit index in $BA.

; Token high three bits choose a little-endian string-group pointer at $E0D9. Low five bits skip that many $FF-terminated strings. Upload the selected tile string and advance the PPU text cursor by its length. Source is trusted to contain terminators.
; Scan through one $FF terminator and advance the source pointer; repeat until the token ordinal reaches zero.
; Synchronize before PPU access and stream tiles until $FF. A zero tile also falls through to completion because the write is followed by BNE; preserve that encoded behavior.
; Read a big-endian nametable destination from the descriptor at $88/$89, then advance the descriptor by two bytes.
; Display $30+1 as three decimal digits beside a six-byte fixed descriptor. Suppress the hundreds digit with tile $FC when zero; this displayed-stage value is distinct from the loader index $03D0.
; Repeated subtraction divides unsigned A into hundreds in Y, tens in X and units in A. No decimal-mode arithmetic is used.
; With rendering disabled, build a ten-tile-wide panel from constant and ascending tile rows, then its horizontal borders. Restore rendering after construction.
; Write the left corner, eight repeated center tiles and the right corner, then move the destination down one nametable row.
; Select blank tile $FC and share the ten-tile constant-row writer.
; Fill ten tiles with Y and advance the nametable destination using the shared pointer helper.
; Write ten incrementing tile IDs starting at Y; advance the nametable destination after the row.
; Set the PPU destination through the common address helper, then emit ten copies of tile $AC. X counts writes; Y retains the tile value.
; Add 32 to the little-endian destination at $A0/$A1, preserving carry into the high byte.
; Reset PPU address latch and write the big-endian hardware address from the little-endian RAM destination $A0/$A1.
; Initialize eight OAM records starting at $0218. A negative mode at $09 selects Y=$BB; otherwise Y=$F8 hides the sprites. Set tile=$FF and X=$FC; attributes are retained.
; Choose strip destination $2A40 and clear low palette bits of eight attribute cells. Share the alternating tile-strip renderer.
; Choose strip destination $2B80 and clear high palette bits of eight attribute cells. Then draw two rows of alternating tile pairs.
; Write 32 repetitions of tile Y followed by tile A. Destination and PPU increment mode are established by the caller.

; Convert coarse player coordinates and scroll into the collision/attribute cell index at $05E4, quadrant at $05E6 and two-bit mask at $05E5. Four quadrant positions correspond to shifts of the base mask $03.

; Clear a 32-tile interface row, initialize its attribute buffer and draw health and owned special-item indicators. Inventory icons may be written immediately or queued for NMI according to the frame mode sign.
; Re-enter the inventory-column renderer after item consumption; initialize its palette mask and column count.

; For each inventory column, gather three ownership bits and select tile/attribute values. Patch one two-bit attribute quadrant while retaining other quadrants; queue the changed attribute slice when rendering is active.

; Six classified inventory attribute bytes indexed by the three-bit ownership value at $8BF6. The effect producers explicitly encode values 6/7 as well as 1..5. For 6/7 this consumer reads the following established code bytes $A9,$10 at $8C3C/$8C3D as attributes. Natural production of these values remains unresolved; keep the existing code/data boundary.
; Select the first special icon tile pair and destination. The shared queue sets a numeric-upload request for NMI.
; Select the second special icon tile pair and destination; share the same queued numeric renderer.
; Select the third special icon tile pair and destination; share the same queued numeric renderer.
; Store destination/tile parameters and set request bits $90 before waiting for frame service.
; A/X/Y supply destination low byte, tile parameter and nametable high byte. Queue the special display update and wait for frame service.
; Load the destination from $A0/$A1. Entry $8C66 instead accepts high byte Y and low byte A; X supplies four consecutive tile IDs.
; Write two adjacent tile IDs, then the next two IDs one nametable row down. Return X advanced by four. The source uses nested JSR fallthrough to share each two-tile row.
; Write the low PPU address byte and emit two ascending tile IDs. Caller has already written the high address byte.
; At attribute-buffer index $BB, retain bits selected by mask $B1 and OR the replacement bits $B0. The caller positions those bits in the desired quadrant.

; Obtain maximum health capacity from the shared helper and clamp current health to ten. Build a centered sequence of two-by-two meter tiles, choosing empty/full attributes from the capacity minus current health. Active rendering queues tile and attribute changes for NMI.

; Two ten-byte health-meter lookup arrays at CPU $8D13 and $8D1D. The first supplies tile bases; the second supplies attribute values. DrawHealthMeter indexes by capacity position. The preceding negative branch is always taken on loop underflow, so there is no instruction fallthrough.
; Return the low health nibble, clamped to ten units. The high nibble is ignored by this display helper.
; Request ten attribute bytes beginning at buffer index $6A. This index encodes the second nametable and its $2A attribute offset.
; Across frame boundaries, fill three 64-byte ranges at $2AC0/$2B00/$2B40 with blank tile $FC.
; Select high destination byte $2B and share the 64-byte blank range writer.
; X/Y supply low/high destination bytes. Write 64 copies of blank tile $FC.
; Write A to every fourth palette-buffer entry, from slot $1C down through zero.
; Supply X=$80 to the following PPU setup entry; remaining arguments come from the caller.
; Clear attribute bytes from index X down through zero. The caller chooses the exact inclusive range.
; Four stage selectors share each packed byte at $E3A3. Extract the relevant two-bit field, save it at $06 and pass it to the CNROM bank-selection helper.

; Scan zero-terminated two-byte record lists from $E40B until the stage index is reached. Keep its pointer at $9E/$9F; count records using a separate cursor $A0/$A1. No runtime entity reachability follows merely from this list.
; Increment the little-endian entity-source pointer at $9E/$9F.

; Initialize at most five 32-byte entity records starting at RAM $0400. Each two-byte descriptor supplies packed coordinates/type/flags; zero terminates the list. Write status, type, timer, coordinates and auxiliary fields, then consume two source bytes. Exact per-type behavior remains for redirect.
; Shared entry using the caller-supplied slot pointer and cap. Stop at cap zero or list terminator; otherwise decode the next entity descriptor.
; When exactly one source entity remains, inspect the stage bitmap at $DD80 and optionally set status bit $04. This is a special-case flag; its gameplay meaning remains unresolved.

; Record offsets: +0 status=$C0 plus flags; +1 descriptor byte shifted right; +2 timer=$08; +7/+8 and +$18 cleared; +$0A one coordinate; +$1C/+$1D set to one; +$1E other coordinate; +$1F low descriptor flag. Type $0E also sets status bits 0/1.
; Consume the two-byte source record, increment the initialized count, decrement remaining count, and advance destination by 32 bytes. The five-slot cap prevents destination low-byte overflow.
; Return stage/8 in X and stage modulo 8 in $B0 for stage-indexed bitmaps.

; Select four tile-property bytes from the CHR selector, then decode the stage map at $EBE9 + stage*96. Expand compressed descriptors into tile rows, render nametables and pack collision/attribute fields. The following helpers share the pointer and row scratch contract.
; For each source descriptor, multiply its tile index by four and point into the expansion table at $E7FD. Copy a four-byte expansion block into the row workspace, then consume the descriptor.
; Toggle row phase to pack alternating attribute halves, advance the attribute-cell index as needed and reuse the $0750 workspace for subsequent rows.
; Select a stage-specific pointer from split low/high tables at $DD88/$DDA8. A zero pair terminates four-byte patch records. Decode cell/quadrant and replace only its two collision bits at RAM $0300.
; For each of sixteen expanded cells, use the selected property bit to produce a collision bit. Pack it into the proper two-bit position of the RAM $0300 collision grid, retaining the other fields.
; Rotate the clear mask and replacement bits twice for each quadrant index in X. Zero leaves the low pair selected.

; Convert sixteen expanded cell IDs into 2x2 tile patterns. Each cell produces base*4|$80, then offsets +2/+1/+3 in the two 32-tile rows. Advance the source by one byte and destination by two; flush the tile buffer unless both nametables are complete.

; Disable rendering and upload 64 tiles from $0760 to the current nametable destination. Advance by $40 bytes. After fifteen blocks switch from $2000 to $2800 and allow nine more blocks; $07 tracks completion.
; Copy four bytes from source pointer $A8/$A9 to destination $AA/$AB, in descending index order. Entry $90CA instead accepts an inclusive maximum index in Y.
; Copy source to destination from Y down through zero. The caller chooses both pointers and the inclusive byte index.
; Set map workspace destination pointer $AA/$AB to $0740.
; Set expansion source pointer $A8/$A9 to $0750.
; Set tile expansion destination pointer $A4/$A5 to $0760.
; Shift A left twice, carrying both high bits into $A9. Caller initializes the high accumulator before forming the expansion-table pointer.

; Select a replacement-rule group by current CHR selector. Each three-byte rule compares corresponding cells in two work rows and replaces the second value when both match. Negative bytes terminate groups. For replaced cells, palette quadrant $03 is changed to $02 while other quadrants are retained.
; Walk rule triples for the current cell. A negative sentinel advances to the next of sixteen cell positions; a matched pair selects the replacement byte.
; Store the replacement, derive its attribute-cell index and quadrant from row phase and cell parity, then replace a fully set two-bit palette field with binary 10.

; Clear both attribute buffers, locate the stage record in the variable-length stream at $F7E9, then expand palette runs into nametable attribute quadrants. Bytes $C0..$FF redirect to the stage record in their low five bits.
; Skip a variable-length record: positive tokens occupy one byte; negative tokens below $C0 occupy two. Zero and stage redirects end the record.
; Redirect tokens restart record selection from the stream origin. Otherwise initialize the destination at $0640 and begin quadrant expansion.

; Zero ends this stage. A positive token encodes palette in low two bits and length in upper six. A negative nonredirect token carries palette bits 4/5 and an extra-repeat bit, followed by an explicit length byte.

; Place nonzero palette bits into the quadrant selected by logical tile position. Positions 0..31 cross two half-row groups; destination advancement accounts for the attribute-byte layout. Zero palette runs only advance because buffers were cleared.
; Clear 128 bytes spanning the two 64-byte attribute buffers.
; Increment little-endian source pointer $A0/$A1.
; Increment little-endian attribute destination pointer $A2/$A3.
; Nested fallthrough executes the increment helper twice, advancing $A4/$A5 by two.
; Increment little-endian tile destination pointer $A4/$A5.
; Nested JSR fallthrough advances $AA/$AB four times. The two-byte entry below is also shared.
; Nested fallthrough advances $AA/$AB twice.
; Increment little-endian map workspace pointer $AA/$AB.
; Clear exactly 100 bytes at RAM $0300, the packed collision grid used by stage decoding and movement.
; Clear $0500..$05A7 and reset its auxiliary counter $072B. This is separate from the five 32-byte primary entity records.
; Clear five 32-byte records at RAM $0400..$049F.
; Clear the six bytes $03F4..$03F9 and return A=0. Their individual gameplay meanings remain unresolved.
; Select RAM $0640 and copy 64 bytes from the pointer at $8C/$8D.
; Select RAM $0680, sharing the same 64-byte indirect copy.
; Preset the common OAM hide loop to X=$7E and Y=32. Preserve the unusual starting byte offset literally.

; Write $F0 to alternating OAM offsets while stepping X backward four bytes per iteration. Y counts pairs of fields, so caller must choose alignment/count; fields not selected by that stride remain intact.
; Service frames until bit 7 of the packed controller byte becomes set. This tests sampled state, not a newly detected edge.
; Service frames until bit 7 of the packed controller byte clears; the complementary wait supports release/press sequencing.
; A/X supply source low/high address. Copy exactly 32 bytes into the palette buffer. The inner entry uses already initialized source, count and destination index.
; Fill all 32 palette slots with $0F, preparing a black screen for the next upload.

; Display lookup/descriptor area. Consumers include shared palette groups, text descriptors, item-name selectors and capacity/row-count arrays used by DrawCharacterStatusScreen. Repeated $AA/$55 patterns are attribute-like values. Exact internal subtable extents remain unresolved; retain generic data boundaries.

; Start a gameplay iteration by recording scroll origin and deriving the player collision cell. Filter contradictory controller directions, mix input into the random seed and process inventory/status input before player effects, damage, attacks and movement.

; Owned item bits 0/1 act only at aligned coordinates and only after changing coarse position. Bit 0 periodically restores health up to the capacity; bit 1 calls an auxiliary effect spawner. Exact item names remain unresolved.
; Save the new coarse position so standing still cannot repeatedly trigger the movement-based item effects.
; Every tenth eligible position change, compare health against capacity and restore one unit if below it. Update the health meter after clamping to ten.
; Persistent item bit 1 invokes the shared effect preparation/spawn helpers. Its visible effect remains unresolved.

; A negative special-object flag enables an axis-aligned proximity test against the coordinates stored in the final OAM record. Both absolute coordinate differences must be below 13. On collection set state bit $20, clear the object flag, move its coordinates off screen and request sound $1B.
; Combine pending hit state with the current damage byte. Persistent item bit 2 alters this path; without it, low pending bits become damage magnitude plus the active flag.

; Apply active damage only before its processed bit is set. Set player state bit $10, subtract the low-nibble damage from health and mark lethal underflow/zero with $80. Trigger the appropriate sound, redraw health and begin a 32-frame hit response.
; Set a 32-frame effect timer and hit-response state; change the first auxiliary sprite attribute.
; Animate the hit effect while its state bit is set. At timer expiry clear it and hide the auxiliary sprite. Negative health enters death handling; surviving players clear damage state.

; Remove the nonattack control bit before testing held input. A latch prevents repeated attack creation until release; choose one of two four-byte projectile records at $05F0/$05F4 according to equipment and availability.
; Latch the new press and choose the first projectile record, optionally falling through to the second. Equipment can require both slots free or change the chosen projectile parameters.

; Write projectile status, equipment-selected type, directional/speed byte and lifetime into the four-byte slot. The high status bits control normal versus paired sprite handling. Sound depends on attack mode.
; At a grid-aligned position, clear remembered movement, set the attack state, initialize its animation timer and request the attack pose.
; While attack state bit $40 is set, decrement its timer and defer movement until expiry. Then restore the walking animation fields and continue input processing.
; With no new direction, continue only the remembered directions that have not reached a 16-pixel grid boundary. New direction input is tested against aligned collision cells before choosing an axis.
; Separate horizontal controller bits from vertical bits. If one axis is blocked, preserve a remembered direction on the other axis; otherwise choose the appropriate directional movement branch.

; Set the up-facing animation fields, test the previous collision row, and decrement screen Y. Near the upper scroll threshold, move the scroll origin instead and record scroll direction. Boundaries and solid cells cancel movement.
; Set right-facing fields and test the adjacent horizontal collision quadrant. Increment screen X up to $F0; a blocked cell keeps the position unchanged.
; Set down-facing animation fields and test the next collision row. Increment screen Y or advance scrolling beyond its threshold. Clamp screen Y to $B0 at the final scroll boundary.
; Store the signed scroll-step indicator and new scroll origin, then update the player animation.
; Set left-facing fields, test the adjacent collision quadrant and decrement screen X unless already zero.
; Advance the player animation after an accepted movement step, then remember the active direction nibble.
; Refresh the current pose even when collision or a screen boundary prevents movement.

; Place the player sprite group, service the shared entity workspace, then update each active projectile through a four-byte temporary record. Finally recompute the 16-bit world Y coordinate from screen Y plus scroll origin and continue gameplay processing.
; Copy one selected four-byte projectile slot backward into zero-page $10..$13 for the shared updater.
; Copy the updated four-byte temporary record back into the selected projectile slot.
; Only test at a 16-pixel world-Y boundary. Above the first collision row return carry set; otherwise select the previous packed row and extract its solid bit into carry.
; Read the selected packed collision cell, mask the player quadrant, shift it into bit zero and return that bit in carry. A is cleared on return.
; At aligned world Y, reject movement beyond collision index $5B or inspect the next row. Between grid boundaries return carry clear. Preserve the encoded boundary-return flags.
; Only test at an aligned screen X. Select the previous two-bit quadrant, crossing to the previous packed byte when quadrant zero wraps.
; Only test at aligned screen X. Select the next two-bit quadrant, crossing to the next packed byte after quadrant three.
; Mask and normalize the adjacent two-bit cell; return its low collision bit in carry and A=0.
; Return (screen Y plus scroll origin) modulo 16, used to continue movement until cell alignment.
; Return screen X modulo 16.

; Temporary fields $10..$13 contain status/type/direction-speed/lifetime. Select OAM group $7C or $84 from status, initialize its pose on first use, otherwise test collision and advance along its direction. A paired mode controls four sprites; expired or out-of-bounds projectiles are hidden.
; High nibble of direction-speed is pixel step size. Normal projectiles query collision and decrement lifetime; paired mode shares motion while bypassing that ordinary lifetime path.
; Subtract the step from OAM Y. Keep the second sprite eight pixels below unless clipped at $B7; paired mode mirrors the coordinate into the other sprite column.
; Add the step to OAM Y and share vertical clipping/placement.
; Add the step to OAM X, rejecting positions at/after $F8. Update the trailing sprite column and mirror extra fields for paired mode.
; Subtract the step from OAM X; unsigned wrap or an off-screen starting position hides the projectile.
; Paired mode hides both OAM groups; otherwise hide the selected pair. Set their Y to $F8, clear attributes and retain only status bit $20 in the projectile record.
; Hide two vertically spaced OAM records and clear their attributes, then clear active state while preserving the retained status bit.
; Retain status bit $20 while clearing active projectile state.

; Choose the OAM pair and directional tile IDs/flip attributes. Direction-indexed offsets place it beside the player; clipping hides individual sprites. Paired mode uses its separate four-sprite descriptor.
; Apply the directional attributes and offset from the player, clipping the vertical tail when it leaves the playfield.
; Apply directional attributes and horizontal offset; clip the right-hand sprite when it exceeds the visible range.
; Set status bit $10 after initial sprite placement.
; Copy four tile/attribute pairs from the fixed descriptor and choose a direction-dependent player-relative offset, then place a 2x2 sprite group.
; Two tile/attribute pairs repeated for the paired-projectile sprite descriptor. InitializePairedProjectileSprites copies these fields into four OAM records; positions are calculated separately.
; X/Y supply screen position. Position the four OAM records as two columns and two rows, eight pixels apart; an invalid top Y is moved to $F0.

; Direction-dependent signed coordinate offsets for projectile placement. InitializeProjectileSprites and InitializePairedProjectileSprites read the tuples relative to the player. Exact individual tuple boundaries follow their indexed consumers.

; Choose a leading sprite according to direction, add a four-pixel center offset and scroll origin, encode the collision-grid position, then call the shared cell query. Return the selected solid bit in carry.
; Shared entry with encoded position already prepared; query the packed grid and expose the low solid bit to the caller.

; Decrement the animation timer. Depending on mode, choose walking, attack or scripted sequence frames. Scripted frame $FF reports completion in carry; other paths return carry clear. Frame IDs are passed to the shared sprite-pattern writer.
; Set a twelve-frame pose timer and select the attack-facing pattern from the direction table.
; Timed player animation bytes consumed by the incrementing index at $9B32. The repeated four-byte pattern is $00,$04,$02,$84, followed by $09,$FF. Do not interpret it as three-byte records.
; Start the established animation/hide iteration at X=0.
; Convert the one-hot player-facing byte into a two-byte table index, then prepare the 2x2 pattern writer at OAM offset $50.
; Set the shared sprite writer dimensions to two by two and obtain the selected pattern ID from $9C00. Caller supplies the directional/animation index in X.
; Place the four OAM records at $0250 as a 2x2 player sprite, eight pixels apart. Screen X is $0F and screen Y is $0C; the hit-response timer can blink each row off screen.
; When the hit-response timer is active, alternate visible Y with hidden Y=$F0 according to timer parity.
; Write four ascending tile IDs to OAM tile fields, stepping by four-byte sprite records.
; Decrement walking timer and change pose only at expiry.
; Reset the timer to six, toggle animation bit zero and use the directional pattern writer.
; Directional player sprite-pattern lookup. SelectDirectionalPlayerPattern and walking/attack helpers select pattern IDs from this bounded area; low-valued entries are data between routines.

; Pause ordinary gameplay and show the inventory cursor. Horizontal selection wraps over the inventory capacity. A latch prevents repeated held-button steps; confirm consumes the selected item, while cancel hides the menu sprites and returns to gameplay.
; Choose forward/backward from the controller bit, wrap the index and set the directional latch. The selected column maps to a 16-pixel cursor X step and sound $2E.
; Hide four menu sprite records at OAM $0208 by writing Y=$F8.

; Collect the three ownership bits at the selected column. Nonzero values index split low/high handler tables at $9CF5/$9CFC. Remove the consumed inventory entry, redraw the interface and jump to the selected item handler.

; Seven low bytes followed by seven high bytes form the item-handler address table. UseSelectedInventoryItem accepts nonzero ownership selectors 1..7; it adds that selector to the encoded table bases, combines the bytes and jumps indirectly. Address values are hypotheses only outside this independently established dispatch contract.
; Play sound $24, restore health to calculated capacity and redraw the meter.
; Set equipment state bit $40. Its precise item name is unresolved.
; Play sound $1F and scan five active entity records. Exclude type $0F; subtract two from field +4 and set status bit $10 when depleted. Finish with the $E0 screen-emphasis effect.
; Play sound $21 and set bit $80 of field +$18 on active entity types $10..$14. Finish with the $20 screen-emphasis effect; the resulting entity behavior remains unresolved.
; Play sound $20 and mark active entity types $06/$08/$09/$0A with status bit $10. Finish with the $80 screen-emphasis effect.
; Play sound $22 and divide field +4 of each active entity by four. Mark depleted records with status bit $10. This handler does not run the emphasis effect.
; Initialize the entity pointer at $0400 and loop count five. Entity records are 32 bytes apart.
; Tail-call the shared handler at $C2FE. Its item-specific behavior is explained at that destination.
; Calculate capacity from the upgrade count and store it as current health.

; A type-indexed flag byte supplies a high-nibble sprite value. Zero high nibble leaves the sprite unchanged; otherwise shift it and OR $F0 before storing.

; Choose horizontal or vertical velocity storage from direction bits; encode sign with bit 7 and clear companion fractional fields.

The pointers identify records, not code. Repeated records support storage structure without establishing each field meaning. Later directional velocity pairs ($BB97/$BBA1), paired initialization flags ($BBB5), type/sprite flags ($BBC9/$BBD5), animation bytes ($BBE1), collision offsets ($BC01/$BC05) and six extents ($BC09) have separate consumers. Generic subformat uncertainty is retained for unproved fields.

; Reset the stack, sprite-zero mode, scroll and transient state. Restore health capacity, decrement lives and redraw interface. Remaining lives restart stage gameplay; zero lives reduce the title continuation counter and return to the title menu.

After four loops, display the ending sequence; otherwise enter supported stage initialization. This entry establishes the preconditions used in artificial progression tests.

; Clear the display and attributes, load interface palette/CHR bank, render the ending descriptor and wait through bounded delays. Then show the character status screen and enter a permanent branch loop.

; Clear RAM pages downward using indirect writes. Special page-zero/page-one bounds preserve the chosen startup/stack areas; the last zero-page range is initialized with $CC. This routine intentionally does not clear every RAM byte.

; Eight signed coordinate deltas. The transition builder walks X from 7 downward, consuming two deltas for each of four OAM sprites.

; Advance X by four bytes to the next sprite record.

; Add the half-group offset to the OAM record index and write one screen X to the selected pair.
; Select three column groups and share the repeated column placement helper.
; Place two rows eight pixels apart. Y at/after $BB becomes hidden $F0. The shared row helper writes two sprite columns.

; Write a three-record row, advance by eight pixels, then repeat for the next row.
; Write the same Y to OAM records at offsets 0,8,16 from X.
; Place rows for the first allocated group, then place the second when its OAM offset is nonzero.

; Show lives minus one, clamped to five icons, as two rows of tile pairs. Zero lives returns without drawing. Remaining slots are blanked with tile $FC.

; Scan secondary 24-byte records, reserve a nonnegative/free status with $80 and return its offset in Y with carry clear. The counter examines seven slots; carry set reports none available.
; Scan seven OAM groups starting at offset $8C with stride sixteen. Attribute bit $08 marks allocation; claim the first free group and return carry clear, otherwise carry set.
; Scan seven single-record candidates from OAM offset $60 with stride four, sharing the allocation-bit protocol.
; Save the stride, test each candidate attribute bit $08 and claim the first free one. Y returns the chosen OAM offset.
; Clear the upload phase, read PPUSTATUS and wait for NMI to set the phase after OAM/PPU service. Clear audio pending on completion. The shared loop count is one in this entry.
; Fill X bytes with A through ($A0),Y, advancing Y with byte wrap. X=0 means 256 writes, not an empty operation.
; For all 64 OAM records, set Y=$F8 and clear attributes, thereby releasing allocation flags. Tile and X bytes are retained.
; Synchronize, blacken the palette, synchronize again, hide/release sprites and clear both nametable tile areas to blank $FC.
; Choose blank tile $FC, then share the two-nametable fill sequence.
; Save tile A, fill the $2000 nametable and then $2800 while rendering is disabled. Each fill writes 960 tiles and leaves attributes separate.
; Synchronize, disable rendering and select $2000 before sharing the 960-tile fill loop.
; Initial X=$C0 and Y=4 produce 192+256+256+256 writes. Restore the mask and scroll after the tile area, preserving the attribute bytes.

; Scratch $B0/$B1 gives width/height, $A0/$A1 source and $A2/$A3 destination. Copy rows, advance source by width and destination by 32, then restore PPU state. Zero byte counts wrap to 256 iterations.
; Scratch $B0 is the tile, $B1/$B2 width/height and $A2/$A3 destination. Fill each row, advance destination by 32 and fall through into PPU cleanup. Zero byte counts wrap to 256 iterations.
; Use the frame scroll marker at $02 to choose the temporary nametable bit and vertical scroll, then restore mirrored PPU control. Both PPUSCROLL writes follow a PPUSTATUS latch reset.
; A is the effective CHR selector 0..3. Write it through the matching byte in the $8000 bank-value table, avoiding CNROM bus-conflict changes to the selected value. PRG remains fixed.
; Mark audio state negative and tail-call the audio frame engine.
; Queue zero for both the sound-effect and music request paths.
; Preserve effect selector A across a frame wait, then submit it to the priority-aware sound-effect request path.
; Use the current shared byte index to read the full 256-byte scalar table, incrementing the index before returning the saved-index value. No generator or probability distribution is implied.

; Full 256-byte scalar lookup addressed by a wrapping byte index. Two consumers establish the complete extent. The established name is retained, but no exact generator or natural probability distribution has been recovered.
; Accept pending music/effect selectors, advance their channel streams and update APU registers. Enable the four non-DMC channels; this engine does not claim sampled DMC playback.

; Process two request sets (music and effects). Negative request bytes carry selectors; effect priority compares against the retained request. Each selector chooses an eight-byte directory of four stream pointers. Nonzero pointers initialize 16-byte channel state records and their private stack pointers.
; Mask selector to six bits, compute directory address and inspect its four pointer pairs. Clear the active-channel mask before enabling each nonzero stream.
; A nonzero little-endian stream pointer initializes that channel timer, flags, private stack pointer and stream address; zero leaves it inactive.

; For each of four hardware channels, advance both music and effect streams whose channel bits are active. Expired timers parse commands until a note/rest or deactivation. Effects take output priority over music for an active channel; otherwise silence it.

; Load the current channel stream pointer. Zero and bytes $C0..$FF are commands; other bytes are note/duration events. Commands may alter or terminate the stream and parsing continues only while the channel mask remains active.
; Prefer an active effect stream, else active music, else silence the hardware channel. This is channel-local priority, separate from request priority.
; AND A with the channel bit indexed by the hardware-channel counter.
; Return music or effect active-channel mask according to the current stream-set index.
; Patch a state flag field at the current channel base using mask Y and value X. The alternate entry below permits an additional byte offset in A.
; Add field offset A to the channel-state base, preserve old bits selected by Y and OR replacement X.
; Return the byte at the current audio stream pointer with Y=0.
; Return hardware channel number times four in X, selecting the $4000-register group and its RAM mirror.
; Save the control byte, select its high-nibble class and use the inline dispatch helper. The following inline table is data consumed through the popped return address, not executable fallthrough.

; Sixteen little-endian high-nibble command targets for the audio inline dispatcher. DispatchInlineAudioPointer consumes them through the caller return-address bias and bypasses these bytes as CPU instructions.
; Decode $C0..$CF controls: low-nibble flag fields, mapped duty/control values, an explicit flag set, or toggling channel flag $04. Advance the stream once after ordinary controls.
; Four duty/control bit patterns $00,$40,$80,$C0. The class-C audio control handler indexes them to replace high flag bits.
; For selectors below $D4, set the stream-set duration-bank index. Higher selectors patch the low nibble of channel field +6; advance past the control.

; Set the high nibble of field +4, then consume two parameter bytes. Their low nibbles select envelope-program offsets; parameter bit $80 controls channel flag $08. Triangle-channel handling stores the second parameter separately.
; Use the saved control low nibble for a second inline dispatch table. The table words following the JSR are stream-dispatch metadata, not CPU opcodes.

; Sixteen little-endian low-nibble audio command targets, consumed by the second inline dispatcher. Handler semantics are documented at the target routines; the table itself is not executable fallthrough.
; Read a little-endian pointer from the following two bytes and replace the channel stream address.
; Toggle channel flag $02. One phase skips a three-byte control record; the other takes the absolute stream jump.

; Initialize the upper nibble of channel field +6 from the command count only when zero, then subtract one count. Nonzero remaining count takes the absolute stream jump; zero skips its pointer operand.

; Temporarily switch the CPU stack to this channel private stack pointer, push the post-command stream pointer and install the target pointer. Save the private stack position and restore the real CPU stack before RTS. No interrupt-state assumption beyond the calling audio engine is invented.
; Switch to the channel private stack, pop the saved stream pointer and restore the real CPU stack. This is the inverse of the audio substream call.
; Save the private stack pointer back to channel state and restore the engine caller stack pointer.
; Clear the current hardware-channel bit from the music/effect active mask. If effects become entirely inactive, set its priority sentinel to $FF.
; Read the two bytes following the current command; return low byte in $D7 and high byte in A.
; Advance the current channel stream pointer by three, covering control plus 16-bit operand.
; Add A to channel stream low byte and propagate carry to high byte.
; Convert the parameter low nibble to an eight-byte envelope-program offset and store it in the selected envelope state record.
; Install the absolute audio stream target with low byte $D7 and high byte A.
; Patch channel field +4 with value A and mask Y, then advance the control stream by one.
; Set channel flag $10 while retaining all other flags.
; Apply the supplied flag value/mask then advance the stream.
; Advance the current stream past a one-byte control.

; Decode duration/note fields, consume the event byte and restart the relevant envelope state unless channel hold flag $10 suppresses it. Triangle uses only one envelope state; other channels restart two.

; Set envelope restart bit $80 in the selected $0100-based envelope state record.
; Four duration-bank offsets $FF,$0A,$15,$20. DecodeAudioDurationAndPitch combines the selected value with the event high nibble to index duration values; retain the encoded $FF bias.

; Choose music/effect channel state from the supplied set offset. Rest flags silence the channel. Otherwise tick envelopes, form volume/duty or triangle control, compute tonal/noise period and update only changed APU registers through mirrors.

; Use envelope values and flags to form the first APU register. Triangle control comes from its dedicated saved parameter on the pending transition; other channels combine duty bits, constant-volume mode and limited envelope amplitude.

; Tonal channels combine note/octave into a period-table index, then apply the signed envelope-scaled delta with a minimum period of eight. Noise derives its 4-bit period from a clamped envelope adjustment and retains mode bit $80.
; Multiply envelope depth by the current envelope value. High notes halve the delta. Add or subtract from the base timer according to flag $08, clamping descending periods at eight.
; Clamp envelope contribution, add/subtract it from the note nibble and saturate to 0..15. Combine it with the retained noise mode bit.
; Optional flag $04 subtracts high period plus one from the low period, carrying borrow. Compare low/high results against RAM mirrors before writing $4002/$4003 for the current channel.
; Select a silent first-register value for pulse/noise. Triangle takes its encoded no-write return path here; preserve that behavior.
; Compare against the first-register RAM mirror and write hardware only when the value changes.
; Return the high nibble of channel field +4.
; Set pending bit $80 and store the music selector. The frame engine accepts its low six bits.
; Set pending bit $80 and store the effect selector unless the retained priority state rejects it. A zero selector is the shared silence request.
; Initialize APU groups, disable DMC control, configure triangle linear counter and enable the four tone/noise channels. Set the effect priority sentinel and invalidate all register mirrors with $FF.
; Write A to the same register offset in each of the four APU channel groups, then increment the offset.

; On restart reset envelope step; otherwise count down its delay. Step through the eight-byte program selected by its stored offset. Program bits encode delay and a 3-bit value mapped through $CF33; step seven holds the terminal state.
; Decrement the delay; when zero advance the program index unless its terminal step seven has already been reached.
; Combine program base and step, load encoded delay/value, then store the mapped value with its active bit.

; Audio tables include envelope value mapping, channel masks, directory base/stack seeds, duration values, octave offsets and paired timer periods. Audio consumers establish these mechanical roles; exact subdivision of every packed table remains unresolved. Generic data is preserved rather than assigning unsupported schemas.
; Multiply unsigned $D7 by $D8 using eight shift/add iterations. Return the 16-bit result in $DA/$DB; $D7/$D8 are consumed and $D9 holds the shifted multiplicand high byte.

; Large PRG asset-data area. Prior full backing/pattern review and static consumer references are preserved in analysis/round001-data-review.json. Known consumers use envelope programs beginning $D038; stage CHR/palette selectors, entity descriptors, trigger scripts, grouped text and tile maps occupy later addresses. Formats are explained at their code consumers. Their exact complete subtable boundaries and remaining game meanings are unresolved; this entire non-code interval remains generic data, with no unused/fill claim.
; Uniform $FF suffix, bounded by the preceding asset area and the hardware vectors. Static boundary/pattern review supports non-code. Its original padding purpose and generator are not established.

; Three little-endian CPU vectors in hardware order: NMI=$8057, reset=$8004, IRQ/BRK=$80F2. All point into the fixed PRG view. These words are pointer metadata, separate from executable code at their targets.

CNROM selects one bank through SelectCnromChrBank; no tile-by-tile artwork semantics or game-wide CHR-use coverage is claimed.
